title: Dive Into the Mystery and Prepare to Question Everything You See. Netflix Unveils Main Poster and Trailer for 'Delusion'
summary: Dive into the mystery with the newly released trailer for Netflix's Delusion, and prepare to question everything you see (and everything you don’t) this Sept 24.
body_markdown:
Entertainment


27 August 2026


Global


Thailand


Link copied to clipboard


When someone you love becomes someone else, can you still trust what you see?


Netflix has unveiled the official trailer and key art for


Delusion


(ภาพลวงตาย), its highly anticipated original mystery series set in Northeastern Thailand, where the quiet devastation of dementia collides with the chilling local folklore of "Phii Pong." The trailer teases meticulous production design and a rural atmosphere thick with suspicion, daring audiences worldwide to uncover the truth when Delusion premieres globally on September 24.


Delusion


plunges viewers into a chilling mystery set in the quiet district of Chiang Khan, Loei Province. A child's disappearance reawakens something the town has spent over a decade trying to forget and bury. As fear takes hold, the old legend of "Phii Pong" resurfaces, and as the town hunts for someone to blame, the suspicion settles on


Narong (Nu-Surasak Chaiyaat)


, an elderly man whose worsening dementia makes him impossible to defend, and impossible to trust — even by his own family.


This forces his daughter,


Wan (Natapohn Phornprapha)


, a provincial high school teacher, to stand up and fight against the town’s rumor and prove that her father is only a sick man who needs care, not the monster the town has decided he is. But every answer she uncovers only raises more questions, and the closer she gets to the truth, the less she recognizes the people closest to her, the ones she calls family.


Natapohn, Jespipat, and Vachiravit in Their Most Challenging Roles Yet


Beyond its gripping narrative,


Delusion


is anchored by a cast taking on some of the most challenging roles of their acting careers.


Taew-Natapohn Phornprapha


, who plays


Wan,


shared that the character deeply resonates with her real life, particularly the struggles of a generation trying to build their own lives while carrying the anxiety of caring for aging parents. This personal connection fueled her dedication to portraying Wan as authentically as possible. Defining the show's core appeal, she explained: "For me, it’s about 'deception.' It makes the audience question what kind of series they are actually watching — is it a mystery, an investigative thriller, or a profound family drama? But there’s something hidden within that ultimately makes you realize why the story had to be told this way."


Jes-Jespipat Tilapornputt


plays


Pete,


a detective transferred from Bangkok, and is someone who believes only in what evidence can prove and his own eyes can see — not superstition, not rumor, and certainly not fear. Jes revealed the intense preparation behind his role: "I had to study the script heavily because the plot is highly complex with a lot of details. I attended several workshops and spoke with real police officers, both from crime and investigation units and the general detective unit, in order to fully understand the differences between them. Even though this is not my first time playing a police officer in my acting career, it was the first time that I truly understood the differences between investigative and interrogative police duties."


August Vachiravit Paisarnkulwong


takes on the role of


Wat,


the family's beloved youngest son. He admitted to feeling immense pressure stepping into the part: "Working alongside so many top-notch, experienced actors meant I had to do more homework than ever before. I had to dig deep into Wat's background to justify his actions in every single scene. I also went through numerous solo and group workshops to truly understand the character on a deeper level before filming, which really helped me in the most effective ways."


The intense narrative is further elevated by a powerhouse supporting cast, including


Nu-Surasak Chaiyaat


,


Tom-Sirani Yankittikan


,


Suttawat Settakorn, Boombim Samtone,


and rising child star


Tham-Norraphat Nakadumrongchai


, who together make this dark mystery complete and unmissable.


More Than a Mystery: Blurring the Lines Between Belief and Reality


What sets


Delusion


apart from typical mystery series is its artful play with ambiguity. Viewers are left stranded between every possibility, unable to guess the true root of the horror: Is it the supernatural folklore of the Phii Pong? The tragic delusions and memory loss caused by a brain disease like dementia? Or a dark, twisted secret intentionally buried by the family?


Director and co-writer Chayan Laoyodtrakool


explained the vision behind this unique blend: "The core of this story is family dynamics, heavily layered with mystery, crime and investigation, and family drama, which amplifies the emotional weight of the series far beyond expectations. I believe that by the end, viewers will be left with a deeper understanding of human nature; one that's closer to them than they might think.”


Prepare yourself


for


Delusion


, a mystery-thriller that will make you question your own eyes. Join the global search for the truth on September 24, only on Netflix.
